references.text: The same command to bind the Lord's words as a sign on the hand and as a mark between the eyes, given in connection with the Passover feast and the exodus from Egypt.
Repeats the instruction to carry God's words as a sign on the hand and as a mark on the forehead, linked to the deliverance of the firstborn.
A parallel command to bind God's words on the hand and have them as a mark between the eyes, as part of the exhortation to love and obey the Lord.
An encouragement to bind faithfulness and truth around the neck and write them on the tablet of the heart, a similar symbolic act to remember God's guidance.
A command to bind a father's teachings on the heart and tie them around the neck, expressing the same principle of always carrying God's words with you.
An encouragement to bind the words of wisdom on the fingers and write them on the tablet of the heart, similar imagery about internalizing God's teaching.
Jesus notes that the Pharisees make their prayer straps (tefillin) broad, showing how the command in Deuteronomy 6:8 was practiced literally in Jewish tradition.
